title: KCA Cycling Strength and Movement Library
subtitle: 36 workouts • TrainingPeaks reference guide • Version 1.0 • November 2026
intro: Use the code assigned by your KCA coach to find your session. Each category contains six alternatives. Complete only the workouts assigned in TrainingPeaks; the library is not a weekly checklist or a sequence from easiest to hardest.
W1: Allow 8–12 minutes, or longer if needed: 3 minutes easy bike or walking; 8 bodyweight squats; 8 unloaded hip hinges; 5 reverse lunges/side; 8 easy rows or wall push-ups. Before the first heavy lift, perform 3–4 progressively heavier practice sets, for example 8 light reps, 5 moderate reps and 2–3 reps near the working load. Rest 45–90 seconds between practice sets. Add 1–2 light preparation sets before a new loaded pattern. Warm-up sets do not count toward working sets.
W2: Allow 4–5 minutes: 90 seconds marching or easy walking, then 6 squats to a chair, 6 hip hinges, 6 wall push-ups and 6 calf raises. Move gently through the ranges required in the session.

sections.title: How to read your workout
paras: 3 × 5 means three sets of five repetitions. /side means complete the number on each side. Rest is taken after each set unless the session is a circuit. For unilateral exercises, complete both sides before the listed rest; take 15–30 seconds to change sides when needed. Session durations are approximate and include the stated warm-up and normal transitions.

Lifting RPE describes how hard a set feels: RPE 6 ≈ 4 good repetitions left, RPE 7 ≈ 3 left, RPE 8 ≈ 2 left. Reps in reserve means technically sound repetitions, not forced repetitions. Ride RPE uses a separate 0–10 effort scale: 2–3 easy/conversational, 5–6 moderate, 7 hard, 8 very hard but controlled. Do not use ride RPE to select lifting loads.

Use controlled range, stable alignment and normal breathing between repetitions. Brace the trunk for loaded lifts. Finish each set before technique breaks down; no failed reps or maximal testing are needed. Stop an exercise for sharp pain, joint pain, dizziness or altered movement, and report it to your coach. Ordinary muscle effort is different from pain.

sections.title: Choose the appropriate starting level
paras: New lifters: start with 3.1 or a coach-supervised light version of a lifting session. For the first 2–4 weeks use 1–2 sets per exercise, RPE 5–6 and simple squat, hinge, push and pull patterns. Movement quality determines readiness; completing a fixed number of weeks does not automatically qualify an athlete for heavy loading.

Junior athletes: use qualified supervision, equipment that fits and technique-led progression. Begin with light resistance and 1–2 sets of 10–15 controlled reps for basic strength exercises; shorten holds and reduce volume as needed. The heavy prescriptions in category 1 are for athletes whose coach has confirmed readiness, not a default for every junior. No unsupervised heavy barbell work.

Experienced lifters: use the listed prescriptions after familiarization. Main heavy lifts should remain at RPE 7–8, even if that requires a lower load than last week. An athlete's cycling level does not establish lifting experience.

sections.title: Warm-up protocols
sub: Allow 8–12 minutes, or longer if needed: 3 minutes easy bike or walking; 8 bodyweight squats; 8 unloaded hip hinges; 5 reverse lunges/side; 8 easy rows or wall push-ups. Before the first heavy lift, perform 3–4 progressively heavier practice sets, for example 8 light reps, 5 moderate reps and 2–3 reps near the working load. Rest 45–90 seconds between practice sets. Add 1–2 light preparation sets before a new loaded pattern. Warm-up sets do not count toward working sets.
Allow 4–5 minutes: 90 seconds marching or easy walking, then 6 squats to a chair, 6 hip hinges, 6 wall push-ups and 6 calf raises. Move gently through the ranges required in the session.

sections.title: Progression and scheduling
paras: Choose one or two complementary strength sessions and repeat them for 4–6 weeks to track progress. Rotate a session when the goal, equipment or athlete needs change; variety alone is not a progression strategy. Categories 1, 2 and 3 are alternative strength-day options. Do not routinely stack all three.

Heavy lifting: when every prescribed set is clean and the last set is no harder than RPE 7 for two exposures, add the smallest available increment, usually about 2–5%. If RPE exceeds 8 or posture changes, reduce load by 5–10% or finish the exercise early. Keep reps fixed while increasing load.

Endurance lifting: first complete the prescribed repetitions with control. Progress a rep-range exercise to its upper limit, then add a small load and return to the lower limit. For fixed-repetition exercises add the smallest load only when all rounds stay at RPE 6 or below. Do not increase load, rounds and ride volume together.

Bodyweight and core: first improve range and control, then add 1–2 reps per set or 5 seconds to holds. Cap most core holds around 30–40 seconds; then select a harder variation with your coach. Keep pre-ride activation easy instead of progressively making it a fatiguing workout. Stretching progresses through comfortable range, not stronger pain.

Typical preparation block: 2 strength sessions/week on nonconsecutive days, usually with at least 48 hours between them; 1–3 short core sessions as needed; mobility as useful. Start at the lower end when cycling load is high. Keep heavy or unfamiliar leg work at least 48 hours before a priority ride or race, and longer if soreness persists.

Typical competition block: 1 familiar low-volume strength session/week, such as 1.6, adjusted to the race calendar. In a priority race week, reduce or omit lifting if it compromises freshness. Never introduce a new exercise close to an important event.

When lifting and riding share a day, protect the priority session. If cycling performance is the priority, ride first and separate lifting by several hours when practical. Do not lift heavily after a ride that leaves you too fatigued to move well. Short easy rides can pair with strength work. Keep at least one genuinely easy or rest day as needed.

Fatigue adjustment: with mild residual soreness and otherwise normal movement, reduce working sets by roughly one-third to one-half and keep RPE ≤6–7. If soreness changes gait or riding mechanics, or fatigue is unusually high, skip loading and tell your coach. Take an easier week when recovery or ride quality indicates it; do not force scheduled progression.

sections.title: Example assignments
paras: Foundation athlete: Tuesday 3.1; Friday 3.2; one optional 4.1 on another day; 5.1 after selected rides; 6.1 before riding. Start with the beginner volume above.

Experienced preparation block: Tuesday 1.1; Friday 1.2; one optional 4.2; 5.2 or 5.4 as needed. Place key cycling sessions to preserve recovery. These examples are starting structures, not complete cycling plans.
Endurance-focused alternative: Tuesday 2.1; Friday 2.4 instead of the heavy pair. Competition block: one 1.6 early enough before the race, with short familiar activation and optional gentle mobility.

sections.title: TrainingPeaks assignment template
paras: Title: KCA 1.1 | Heavy strength | Squat foundation

Description: Complete KCA 1.1 from the KCA Cycling Strength and Movement Library. Include W1. Use the listed sets and rests; main lifts RPE 7–8 with 2–3 good reps in reserve. Today's adjustment: [standard / reduced sets / exercise substitution]. Library: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_MRvZupO-o-VREkGMy5Bq1AsB0ln8Rqkg_qfAkITI_s/edit

After training, record: exercise, load, sets × reps, last-set RPE, any discomfort and any changes. For dumbbells specify load per hand; for a barbell include the bar. Example: squat 45 kg total, 3 × 5, final set RPE 7, no pain. The next day, note whether soreness affected pedaling.

For combinations, name each code: KCA 1.2 + 4.1. Add the approximate durations together, and reduce overlapping core work if needed. Activation example: KCA 6.3 before intervals; use only one on-bike warm-up if the ride already includes one.

sections.title: Coach notes and evidence
paras: These 36 sessions are KCA programming templates based on established strength-training principles. The exact combinations, doses and activation sequences have not been tested as a single program. Choose loads and exercises around the individual athlete's age, technique, history, equipment, cycling demands and recovery.

Heavy resistance training has improved cycling performance in controlled studies of trained cyclists. This supports including progressive strength work, but does not mean every exercise or endurance circuit produces the same benefit. High-repetition gym work is an option for local work capacity, not a replacement for cycling-specific endurance.

Rønnestad et al. Strength training improves performance and pedaling characteristics in elite cyclists (2015). Controlled trial supporting strength work alongside endurance training. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24862305/

Vikmoen et al. Strength training improves cycling performance, fractional utilization of VO2max and cycling economy in female cyclists (2016). Controlled trial supporting inclusion of strength work in trained female cyclists. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25892654/

Rønnestad et al. In-season strength maintenance training increases well-trained cyclists' performance (2010). Small study supporting reduced-frequency maintenance after a preparation block. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20799042/

NSCA. Youth Resistance Training: Updated Position Statement Paper (2009). Supports qualified supervision, appropriate starting resistance and technique-led progression in youth. https://www.nsca.com/globalassets/about/position-statements/position_stand_youth_resistance_training---2009.pdf

Behm et al. Acute effects of muscle stretching on physical performance, range of motion, and injury incidence in healthy active individuals (2016). Review informing dynamic preparation before riding and the use of longer static holds away from immediate high-force efforts. Stretching does not guarantee injury prevention. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26642915/

cats.name: Heavy lifting
cats.intro: Develop maximal force with controlled, technically sound repetitions. Experienced lifters only at the listed load. Complete straight sets in order; do not circuit the main lifts. Main lifts: RPE 7–8 (2–3 reps in reserve), 2–3 minutes rest. Accessories: RPE 7, 60–90 seconds rest. Lower under control for about 2 seconds; lift with fast intent without losing position. Use warm-up W1.

cats.name: Muscular endurance lifting
cats.intro: Build local muscular endurance and general work capacity. These sessions complement cycling; they do not replace threshold or endurance work on the bike. Use W1. Unless specified, complete 2 rounds in order, 30–45 seconds between exercises and 2 minutes between rounds. Use light loads at RPE 6–7, with at least 3 reps in reserve. Control the lowering phase for about 2 seconds. These are strength days, not extra recovery sessions.

cats.name: Bodyweight strength
cats.intro: Use bodyweight resistance to build movement skill and practical strength. Start with W2. Unless stated, complete straight sets in order at RPE 6–7; leave 3 good reps in reserve. Rest 60 seconds between sets and exercises, and 15–30 seconds to switch sides. Lower for about 2 seconds. A stable chair, wall, mat or low step may be used; no external weights are required.

cats.name: Core
cats.intro: Develop trunk control while breathing normally. These are add-ons, not maximal abdominal tests. Begin with 1 minute of easy marching and 4 relaxed breaths. Complete 2 rounds in order, 20–30 seconds between drills and 60 seconds between rounds. Take 10–15 seconds to switch sides. Target RPE 5–7; stop each hold before shaking or posture loss. No need to add a second core session if the day's lifting already supplies enough trunk work.

cats.name: Stretching and mobility
cats.intro: Use after riding, after training or separately. Begin with 2 minutes of easy walking if cold. Move within a comfortable range; stretch sensation should be mild, about 2–3/10, with no bouncing, pinching or numbness. Complete drills in order. For static stretches do both sides before the second set, with about 10 seconds to transition. For mobility repetitions, move slowly and pause briefly at the end of the comfortable range. These sessions address range of motion and comfort; they are not a treatment for injury or a guarantee of recovery.

cats.name: Pre-ride activation
cats.intro: Prepare for the ride without creating fatigue. Complete one round of the listed off-bike drills, taking 10–15 seconds between drills and sides; use RPE 2–4. Then complete the on-bike warm-up below the drill list. On-bike minutes are included in the ride, not added a second time. Off-bike activation does not replace easy pedaling. For easy rides, the on-bike warm-up alone may be sufficient. Race and sprint options require prior practice and coach selection; none of the efforts is all-out.

Add 1–2 light preparation sets before a new loaded pattern. Warm-up sets do not count toward working sets.

workouts.name: Squat foundation
workouts.equip: Rack, barbell, dumbbells, cable or band
workouts.focus: Knee-dominant force, unilateral stability and upper-back support.
workouts.adj: Use a goblet squat for the squat pattern and keep RPE 6 if barbell technique is not established.

ex.name: Back squat
ex.note: Brace before descending; keep whole foot planted. Use rack safeties.

ex.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
ex.note: Push hips back; keep weights close and stop before the back rounds.

ex.name: Supported split squat
ex.note: Light hand support; front knee tracks over toes.

ex.name: Seated cable row
ex.note: Pull elbows back without shrugging.

ex.name: Standing calf raise
ex.note: Pause at top; lower heel slowly.

workouts.name: Hinge and posterior chain
workouts.equip: Trap bar, dumbbells, bench, pull-down machine
workouts.focus: Hip extension strength with balanced pushing and pulling.
workouts.adj: Replace the trap bar with kettlebell deadlifts from blocks; keep the same movement quality.

ex.name: Trap-bar deadlift
ex.note: Brace, push the floor away and finish tall without leaning back.

ex.name: Low dumbbell step-up
ex.note: Use a height you can control; avoid pushing off the trailing foot.

ex.name: Dumbbell bench press
ex.note: Keep wrists stacked and shoulder blades supported.

ex.name: Lat pull-down
ex.note: Pull toward upper chest; avoid swinging.

ex.name: Bent-knee seated calf raise
ex.note: Keep pressure through the ball of the foot.

workouts.name: Unilateral strength
workouts.focus: Single-leg force and pelvic control.
workouts.adj: Use a supported floor split squat instead of elevating the rear foot.

ex.name: Rear-foot-elevated split squat
ex.note: Use a low support; keep pelvis level and front foot planted.

ex.name: Barbell or dumbbell hip thrust
ex.note: Finish with glutes; avoid arching the lower back.

ex.name: Hamstring curl machine
ex.note: Keep hips still through the full comfortable range.

ex.name: One-arm dumbbell row
ex.note: Support torso; pull toward hip without rotating.

ex.name: Incline push-up
ex.note: Choose height that leaves 2–3 good reps in reserve.

workouts.name: Machine strength option
workouts.equip: Leg press, hamstring curl, chest press, row, calf machine
workouts.focus: Controlled full-body strength when a barbell setup is unavailable.
workouts.adj: Adjust every machine to the athlete. If it cannot fit properly, choose a free-weight alternative.

ex.name: Leg press
ex.note: Keep pelvis against pad; stop before the lower back curls.

ex.name: Seated hamstring curl
ex.note: Align knee with machine axis and control the return.

ex.name: Chest press machine
ex.note: Set handles near mid-chest height; keep shoulders down.

ex.name: Chest-supported row
ex.note: Keep chest on pad and avoid lifting the chin.

ex.name: Calf raise machine
ex.note: Use a smooth comfortable range; do not bounce.

workouts.name: Full-body MTB support
workouts.focus: Leg force, pulling strength and support for handling the bike.
workouts.adj: Use goblet squats and lighter carries; upper-body work should not cause next-day handling fatigue.

ex.name: Front squat
ex.note: Keep elbows high and brace; use goblet squat if the rack position is uncomfortable.

ex.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
ex.note: Hinge at hips with a long spine.

ex.name: Half-kneeling one-arm cable press
ex.note: Squeeze rear glute; press without twisting.

ex.name: Chest-supported dumbbell row
ex.note: Keep chest supported and shoulders away from ears.

ex.name: Farmer carry
ex.note: Walk tall with a load you can carry without tilting.

workouts.name: In-season maintenance
workouts.equip: Familiar squat or trap-bar setup, dumbbells, row station
workouts.focus: Retain established strength with less total volume.
workouts.adj: For an important race week, coach may reduce to one set per exercise or omit. Do not introduce new lifts.

ex.name: Familiar squat OR trap-bar deadlift
ex.note: Choose the lift already practiced in the current block.

ex.name: Supported split squat
ex.note: Keep each repetition smooth.

ex.name: Cable or dumbbell row
ex.note: Pull without shrugging or rotating.

ex.name: Push-up
ex.note: Use an incline if needed.

ex.name: Calf raise
ex.note: Controlled range; leave plenty in reserve.

workouts.name: Full-body endurance
workouts.focus: General capacity across squat, hinge, push and pull.
workouts.adj: Start with one round if new; progress to the prescribed two rounds before adding load.

ex.name: Goblet squat
ex.note: Keep chest and pelvis stacked.

ex.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
ex.note: Hips back, weights close.

ex.name: Incline push-up
ex.note: Stop before the trunk sags.

ex.name: Cable row
ex.note: Pause briefly with elbows back.

ex.name: Standing calf raise
ex.note: Use a slow full comfortable range.

workouts.name: Single-leg endurance
workouts.focus: Repeated unilateral effort with stable knee and hip alignment.
workouts.adj: Use hand support and bodyweight for lunges and steps; rest 30 seconds when changing legs if needed.

ex.name: Reverse lunge
ex.note: Step back softly and drive through front foot.

ex.name: Low step-up
ex.note: Control the descent; no bounce from trailing leg.

ex.name: Glute bridge
ex.note: Lift through hips without arching.

ex.name: Standing band row
ex.note: Use a secure anchor; keep ribs down.

ex.name: Bent-knee calf raise

workouts.name: Posterior-chain endurance
workouts.focus: Hip and hamstring endurance plus upper-back support.
workouts.adj: Replace curls with 12 glute bridges if no machine; use lower loads if hamstrings remain sore for riding.

ex.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
ex.note: End the hinge when hamstrings limit motion.

ex.name: Hamstring curl machine
ex.note: Keep pelvis still.

ex.name: Dumbbell hip thrust
ex.note: Pause for one second at the top.

ex.name: Chest-supported row
ex.note: Move the arms without lifting chest off pad.

ex.name: Suitcase carry
ex.note: Walk slowly without leaning toward or away from load.

workouts.name: Upper-body trail endurance
workouts.focus: Push, pull, grip and shoulder endurance for sustained bike control.
workouts.adj: Use an easier push-up incline and lighter grip loads; finish with control rather than forearm exhaustion.

ex.name: Incline push-up
ex.note: Keep elbows roughly 30–45 degrees from torso.

ex.name: One-arm dumbbell row
ex.note: Support the free hand and keep trunk still.

ex.name: Band external rotation
ex.note: Elbow at side; rotate outward without turning torso.

ex.name: Farmer carry
ex.note: Stay tall; use short controlled steps.

ex.name: Bodyweight squat
ex.note: Use an easy comfortable depth.

workouts.name: Travel dumbbell endurance
workouts.equip: Pair of dumbbells, stable bench or chair
workouts.focus: Maintain a full-body training stimulus away from the gym.
workouts.adj: If weights are very light, use a 3-second lowering phase rather than rushing or adding endless reps.

ex.name: Dumbbell squat
ex.note: Hold weights at sides; keep feet planted.

ex.name: Dumbbell floor press

ex.name: Supported dumbbell row
ex.note: Keep shoulders and hips square.

ex.name: Standing calf raise
ex.note: Use wall support if balance limits control.

workouts.adj: Override normal circuit rest: 20 sec between exercises, 2 min between rounds, 2 rounds. RPE 6; timed sets never require working to failure.

ex.name: Goblet squat
ex.note: Use a steady pace and stop early if technique declines.

ex.name: Band row
ex.note: Secure the anchor; avoid momentum.

ex.name: Alternating reverse lunge
ex.note: Alternate legs evenly with a controlled step.

ex.name: Wall or incline push-up
ex.note: Choose a height that stays comfortable for the interval.

ex.name: Glute bridge
ex.note: Lift smoothly; keep ribs down.

ex.name: Wall or incline push-up

ex.name: Glute bridge

ex.name: Seated ankle circles
ex.note: Move slowly without forcing the outer range.

workouts.name: Upper back and shoulders
workouts.focus: Thoracic rotation and shoulder mobility after riding posture.
workouts.adj: Shorten the range if the shoulder pinches; skip the painful drill.

ex.name: Side-lying open book
ex.note: Knees stay together as upper arm opens across chest.

ex.name: Quadruped thoracic rotation
ex.note: Hand behind head; rotate through upper back without shifting hips.

ex.name: Doorway chest stretch
ex.note: Use a comfortable arm height and avoid front-shoulder pain.

ex.name: Wall slide
ex.note: Raise forearms without flaring ribs.

workouts.name: Full-body mobility
workouts.focus: A longer session for hips, ankles and upper back.
workouts.adj: For a shorter session, do one set of each drill.

ex.name: Cat-cow
ex.note: Move spine gently with the breath.

ex.name: Half-kneeling hip-flexor stretch
ex.note: Squeeze rear glute; stay tall.

ex.name: Supine hamstring stretch
ex.note: Keep stretch mild behind thigh.

ex.name: Knee-to-wall rocks
ex.note: Heel stays down.

ex.name: Open book
ex.note: Rotate slowly with knees stacked.

ex.name: Doorway chest stretch
ex.note: Keep shoulders relaxed.

workouts.name: Evening gentle mobility
workouts.focus: Comfortable movement and relaxed breathing.
workouts.adj: Keep effort very low. Use supine breathing instead of any uncomfortable position.

ex.name: Supine relaxed breathing
ex.note: Rest calves on a chair if comfortable; do not force breath holds.

ex.name: Supported child's pose
ex.note: Rest chest on a cushion; skip if knees dislike the position.

ex.name: Supine figure-four stretch
ex.note: Relax the jaw and shoulders.

ex.name: Open book
ex.note: Follow the upper hand with your eyes if comfortable.

ex.name: Half-kneeling hip-flexor stretch
ex.note: Use padding under knee.

workouts.name: Everyday ride
workouts.focus: General movement preparation.
workouts.adj: Bike: 8 min easy conversational pedaling at RPE 2–3, increasing cadence gradually.

ex.name: March in place
ex.note: Relax shoulders and gradually increase rhythm.

ex.name: Bodyweight squat
ex.note: Use a comfortable depth.

ex.name: Standing hip hinge
ex.note: Push hips back with spine long.

ex.name: Supported leg swing
ex.note: Keep trunk still; do not kick to end range.

ex.name: Calf raise
ex.note: Move smoothly.

workouts.name: Hip and glute preparation
workouts.focus: Prepare hips for smooth pedal strokes.
workouts.adj: Bike: 5 min easy, then 3 × (20 sec quick relaxed cadence + 40 sec easy), then 2 min easy; use light gearing, no bouncing.

ex.name: Glute bridge
ex.note: Squeeze glutes without arching.

ex.name: Lateral mini-band walk
ex.note: Small steps, toes forward; use no band if unavailable.

ex.name: Supported split squat
ex.note: Keep effort easy.

ex.name: Standing hip hinge
ex.note: Move at hips rather than lower back.

ex.name: Dead bug heel tap
ex.note: Exhale with each heel tap.

workouts.name: Threshold or VO2 session preparation
workouts.focus: Build readiness before a demanding interval workout.
workouts.adj: Bike: 6 min easy, 4 min gradually building to RPE 5, 2 × (30 sec brisk RPE 7 + 90 sec easy), 1 min easy. Use the TrainingPeaks workout's warm-up instead if one is already prescribed.

ex.name: March in place
ex.note: Gradually raise movement rate.

ex.name: Alternating reverse lunge
ex.note: Use a shallow comfortable range.

ex.name: Bodyweight squat
ex.note: Keep repetitions easy.

ex.name: Supported leg swing
ex.note: Stay controlled.

ex.name: Wall push-up
ex.note: Move shoulders through a comfortable range.

workouts.name: XCO race preparation
workouts.equip: Mini-band optional, safe riding area or trainer
workouts.focus: Prepare for race intensity while staying fresh.
workouts.adj: Bike: 8 min easy, 4 min build to RPE 5–6, 3 × (20 sec controlled fast effort at RPE 8 + 100 sec easy), 2 min easy. No maximal starts. Rehearse beforehand; shorten in heat or when prone to fatigue, and time completion near staging.

ex.name: Bodyweight squat
ex.note: Smooth and easy.

ex.name: Reverse lunge
ex.note: Keep pelvis level.

ex.name: Lateral band walk or side step
ex.note: Keep steps short.

ex.name: Incline scapular push-up
ex.note: Straight elbows; let shoulder blades glide.

ex.name: Standing thoracic rotation
ex.note: Rotate gently without forcing hips.

workouts.name: Technical trail ride
workouts.focus: Prepare shoulders, trunk and hips for handling.
workouts.adj: Bike: 7 min easy riding, then 3 min of gentle braking, cornering and standing-position practice in a clear, safe area; no jumps or technical hazards during warm-up.

ex.name: Wall scapular push-up
ex.note: Keep elbows straight.

ex.name: Standing thoracic rotation
ex.note: Turn upper trunk gently.

ex.name: Supported lateral lunge
ex.note: Sit into the hip with foot flat.

ex.name: High-plank shoulder tap at incline
ex.note: Keep trunk steady and effort easy.

ex.name: Wrist circles and hand open/close
ex.note: Use a relaxed pain-free range.

workouts.name: Short travel or cold-morning preparation
workouts.focus: A compact routine before gradually warming on the bike.
workouts.adj: Bike: 9 min easy, then 3 × (15 sec relaxed fast cadence + 45 sec easy). Add easy pedaling if still cold; do not force intensity while stiff.

ex.name: Brisk march
ex.note: Keep movement relaxed.

ex.name: Bodyweight squat
ex.note: Start shallow and increase comfortable range.

ex.name: Alternating reverse lunge
ex.note: Use support if stiff.

ex.name: Arm circles
ex.note: Start small.

ex.name: Calf raise
ex.note: Rise and lower slowly.
